name: Triangulation
short_definition: Pulling a third person, real or made up, into a disagreement between two people, so their supposed opinion wins the argument.
also_called: Central Positioning; Jealousy Manufacturing; Mirror Operation; Triangulation (Positive); Triangulation (Weaponized)

name: Priming / Narrative Seeding
short_definition: Giving someone an interpretation of a person or event before they see it themselves, so what they notice afterward fits that view.
also_called: Institutional Contamination; Narrative Injection; Narrative Seeding; Priming

name: Credibility Theft
short_definition: Credibility theft casts doubt on someone's reliability in advance, so whatever they later report is heard as doubtful before they have said it.
sources: Fricker (2007). Epistemic Injustice Power and the Ethics of Knowing. Oxford University PressOxford. https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198237907.001.0001

name: Interruption Patterns
short_definition: The same people keep getting cut off in group conversations, so their points never get finished while other speakers finish theirs freely.

name: Punishment by Proxy
short_definition: Trouble, coldness or harm lands on someone you care about after a disagreement, so you carry the cost without any direct attack on you.

name: Stochastic Harassment Direction
short_definition: Someone keeps describing a named person in angry terms to a big audience, so some listeners predictably harass them although nobody gives an order.

name: Labeling as Identity Warfare
short_definition: Others pin a fixed defect label on a person, such as 'the difficult one', until everything that person does is read through it.
also_called: Condition-Identity Fusion; Deficit Framing; Institutional Language Framing; Labeling; Name Erosion; Program Naming; Strength Invisibility

name: Scapegoating
short_definition: Blame for a failure shared by many lands on one person, who pays the price while the real cause stays untouched.

name: Flying Monkeys / Proxy Recruitment
short_definition: Friends, relatives or colleagues are drawn in to pass on pressure or criticism, or to report back, for a person who stays out of the room.
also_called: Proxy Recruitment; Flying Monkeys; Parental Amplification; Peer Pressure Weaponization; Proxy Control

name: Smear Campaigns
short_definition: Someone spreads distorted or false stories about a person to people who matter to them, so they are doubted, shunned or not believed before they speak.
also_called: Reputation Poisoning; Reputation Warfare (Post-Separation); Smear Campaign; Reputation Warfare; Smear Campaign (Preemptive); Smear Campaign (Reactive); Untraceable Seeding

name: Silent Coalitions
short_definition: A group leaving one person out through many small, deniable slights, so no single clear incident ever stands out.

name: Pile-Ons / Brigading
short_definition: Many people pile criticism onto one person in a short span, so the sheer volume becomes the problem.
also_called: Brigading; Pile-Ons; Audience Activation; Pressure Accumulation; dogpiling

name: Ostracism
short_definition: A person is left out of invitations, conversations, decisions or information until they end up on the outside of their own group.
sources: Williams (2007). Ostracism. Annual Review of Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.psych.58.110405.085641

name: Golden Child Elevation
short_definition: One family member is held up as the model of excellence, and that standard is used to measure everyone else and find them short.

name: False Consensus / Social Proof Pressure
short_definition: Someone claims that everyone else already agrees, to push one person into going along, whether or not the agreement is real.
also_called: False Consensus; Normative Messaging; Social Proof Pressure; Early Endorsement Seeding; Gaslighting by Consensus; Petition Legitimation; Phantom Endorsement; Phantom Lead; Pluralistic Ignorance Installation; Social Pressure Layering; Social Proof; Social Proof Amplification; Social Proof Engineering; bandwagon effect
sources: Ross et al. (1977). The “false consensus effect”: An egocentric bias in social perception and attribution processes. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-1031(77)90049-X

name: Divide and Conquer
short_definition: Distance or distrust is created between people who might otherwise support one another, so they do not compare notes or act together.
also_called: Wedge Issue Exploitation; Ally Poisoning; Defensive Withdrawal Induction; Manufactured Conflict; Momentum Collapse; Reentry Disruption

name: Social Mapping
short_definition: Identifying the target's relationships and developing a strategy for each.

name: Support System Exhaustion
short_definition: Directing the target to the same resources until they burn out.

name: Identity-Based Isolation
short_definition: Leveraging marginalized identity to enforce silence.

name: Contribution Erasure
short_definition: A person's or group's presence, contributions or history are left out of what is taught, shown or remembered, so absence starts to look like irrelevance.
also_called: Curricular Absence; Legacy Erasure; Predecessor Erasure

name: Repetition as Truth
short_definition: Saying the same claim over and over, with no new evidence, until its familiarity begins to feel like proof.
sources: Hasher et al. (1977). Frequency and the conference of referential validity. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0022-5371(77)80012-1

name: Countering
short_definition: Flatly contradicting someone's account of an event over and over, so the two of you can never agree on what happened.

name: Moving Goalposts
short_definition: Changing what counts as success after you have met the standard that was set, so that you can never quite finish.
also_called: Milestone Migration; Moving the Goalpost; Standards Shifting

name: Thought-Stopping Clichés
short_definition: Stock phrases, said in a closing tone, that end a conversation about a problem before anyone has looked at it.
also_called: "That's Just How It Is"; thought-terminating cliché
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Normalization / Overton Window Manipulation
short_definition: Presenting harmful or hurtful treatment as ordinary and not worth questioning, so that objecting to it seems like the problem.
also_called: Overton Window Manipulation; Normalization; Cycle Perpetuation; Gap Normalization; Institutional Dependency Normalization; Window Shifting

name: Exaggeration
short_definition: Stretching a claim with words like always, never, everyone or nothing, so it sounds bigger and harder to answer than the facts support.

name: Vague Allegations with High Consequences
short_definition: Hinting that unnamed people have complaints about someone, without saying what the complaints are. The claim cannot be checked, answered or corrected.

name: Gotcha Framing
short_definition: Taking an honest, tentative remark and presenting it as a confession, so that being open with someone has a price.

name: False Authority
short_definition: Presenting a personal opinion or bias as neutral fact. Disagreeing then looks like arguing against reality.

name: Aftercare Control
short_definition: Recasting a hurtful act as a kindness after it happened. The person who was hurt begins to doubt their own memory of the harm.

name: Burden of Proof Shifting / Sealioning
short_definition: Pressing someone again and again, in a polite tone, to produce evidence or explanation. It wears them out and does not move toward understanding.
also_called: Burden of Proof Shifting; Sealioning; shifting the burden of proof

name: Forged Screenshots / Edited Evidence
short_definition: Passing off invented or altered messages, images or documents as genuine proof of something that did not happen or was not said.
also_called: Forged Screenshots; Deepfakes; Edited Recordings; Fabricated Evidence; Deepfake Video/Audio

name: Credential-Costuming
short_definition: Wearing a title or affiliation that is invented, stretched or borrowed, so a claim carries more authority than the person's real qualifications support.

name: Platform Migration
short_definition: Steering a conversation from messages or email onto calls, disappearing-message apps or in-person talk when the topic might later be quoted back.

name: Authority Hijack
short_definition: Authority Hijack insists it knows what another person really feels, thinks or meant better than they do, and treats their account as the one to correct.

name: Gish Gallop / Firehose of Falsehood
short_definition: Overwhelming a rival in live debate with a rapid stream of claims, many weak or false, too many to answer one by one.
also_called: AI-Driven Narrative Hijacking; Firehose of Falsehood; Gish Gallop; Memory Flooding; shotgun argumentation
sources: Paul and Matthews (2016). The Russian "Firehose of Falsehood" Propaganda Model: Why It Might Work and Options to Counter It. RAND Corporation. https://doi.org/10.7249/PE198

name: Limited Hangout
short_definition: A limited hangout shares part of the truth or admits a smaller wrong, so it seems fully disclosed while the larger part stays hidden.

name: Pseudo-Profundity / Intellectual Intimidation
short_definition: Pseudo-profundity uses grand, technical or abstract language that sounds deep but explains little, so questioning it seems like admitting you are not clever enough.
sources: Pennycook et al. (2015). On the reception and detection of pseudo-profound bullshit. Judgment and Decision Making. https://doi.org/10.1017/S1930297500006999

name: Semantic Erosion / Meaning Dilution
short_definition: Using a serious word for so many small things that it loses its weight when someone needs it for something real.

name: Dog Whistling / Coded Signaling
short_definition: Words that sound ordinary to most listeners but carry a second, often threatening or exclusionary message for people who know the code.

name: Context Collapse
short_definition: Saving a person's messages, posts or remarks without their context, then bringing them out later at the moment they will do the most damage.
also_called: Context Collapse Exploitation; Evidence Traps; Context Elimination; Context Stripping; Moment Extraction
sources: Marwick and boyd (2010). I tweet honestly, I tweet passionately: Twitter users, context collapse, and the imagined audience. New Media & Society. https://doi.org/10.1177/1461444810365313

name: Revisionist History
short_definition: Changing the agreed account of past events so it matches the story someone prefers now, even though others clearly remember it differently.
also_called: Memory Manipulation; Narrative Editing; Record Inversion; Retconning; Retroactive Recharacterization

name: Word Salad
short_definition: Answering with long, looping language that never reaches a point, so the listener cannot pin anything down.

name: Contradiction Stacking
short_definition: Saying something never happened and then, in the same talk, defending it as justified, so no single answer settles the matter.

name: Pseudo-Logic
short_definition: Defending a claim by pointing back to the claim itself, so no outside fact is ever allowed to test it.

name: Loaded Language
short_definition: Choosing words that carry a verdict, label or insult so that a judgment is made before the facts are discussed.
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Semantic Traps
short_definition: Steering a conversation to the exact wording someone used, so the original concern gets lost in a fight about definitions.

name: Frame Control / False Framing
short_definition: Deciding what a conversation is about, through loaded labels or topic swaps, so that your actual concern has no place to land.
also_called: False Framing; Frame Assassination; PSYOP Message Framing; Frame Control; Community Reframing; Problem Identification (Selective)

name: Ambiguity as Weapon / Strategic Ambiguity
short_definition: Wording a promise, an exclusion or an intention so loosely that several readings stay open, and the useful one is chosen later.
also_called: Ambiguity as Weapon; Strategic Ambiguity; Community Confusion Exploitation; Confidentiality Uncertainty
sources: Eisenberg (1984). Ambiguity as strategy in organizational communication. Communication Monographs. https://doi.org/10.1080/03637758409390197

name: Meta-Gaslighting
short_definition: Answering a person's naming of a harmful pattern by denying it and suggesting that naming it is itself the harm.

name: Double Binds
short_definition: Giving someone demands that contradict each other, so that whatever they choose, they are told they chose wrong.
also_called: Contradictory Expectations; Double Bind Installation; Paradoxical Injunctions
sources: Bateson et al. (1956). Toward a theory of schizophrenia. Behavioral Science. https://doi.org/10.1002/bs.3830010402

name: Bait and Switch
short_definition: Promising or advertising an appealing deal, then swapping in a worse one after the person has committed or given something up.

name: Lying by Omission / Gaslighting by Omission
short_definition: Leaving out information the other person needs for an accurate picture, while everything that is said stays technically true.
also_called: Gaslighting by Omission; Selective Information Sharing; Strategic Incompleteness; Lying by Omission; Information Drip

name: Half-Truth Framing
short_definition: Choosing and arranging statements that are each true so that the listener ends up with a false overall picture.
also_called: Paltering; Selective Disclosure; Selective Truth Weaponization

name: Compartmentalization
short_definition: Keeping information in separate pockets so different people know different parts, and nobody can see enough to notice a problem or ask the right question.
also_called: Confidential Disclosure Seeding; Selective Information Sharing

name: Stonewalling
short_definition: Complete refusal to engage, respond, or resolve.
sources: John Mordechai Gottman (1993). What Predicts Divorce?. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL1982055W

name: Emotional Sequencing
short_definition: Rapidly shifting between emotions to destabilize.
also_called: Emotional Non Sequiturs; Erratic Emotional Behavior

name: Perspecticide
short_definition: The destruction of the target's ability to hold their own point of view.

name: Moral Disengagement
short_definition: Harmful acts are described in ways that make them feel acceptable: necessary, someone else's decision, or deserved by the people they hurt.
sources: Bandura (1999). Moral Disengagement in the Perpetration of Inhumanities. Personality and Social Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr0303_3

name: Retroactive Justification
short_definition: Reasons for a decision appear only after it was made and challenged, and are presented as if they were the reasons all along.

name: Victim Blaming
short_definition: The harmed person is held partly or wholly responsible for what was done to them, through questions or remarks about their choices instead of the other person's actions.
sources: Bandura (1999). Moral Disengagement in the Perpetration of Inhumanities. Personality and Social Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr0303_3; Lerner and Miller (1978). Just world research and the attribution process: Looking back and ahead. Psychological Bulletin. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.85.5.1030

name: Just Asking Questions
short_definition: Accusations or false claims are put as questions, so the claim spreads while the speaker can say they only asked.

name: Motte-and-Bailey
short_definition: A bold claim is made, and when it is challenged the speaker retreats to a modest version anyone would accept, then returns to the bold claim once the challenge passes.
sources: Shackel (2005). THE VACUITY OF POSTMODERNIST METHODOLOGY. Metaphilosophy. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9973.2005.00370.x

name: Narrative Monopoly
short_definition: Controlling the dominant story so alternative accounts can't gain traction.

name: Negging
short_definition: Slipping in a subtle insult, wrapped as a compliment or a joke. You end up feeling a little smaller and a little more eager for approval.

name: Contempt
short_definition: Treating someone with open disgust or superiority. It is aimed at who they are, not at anything they did.
also_called: Curiosity Dismissal; Intellectual Belittling; Microexpressions of Contempt; Projected Disgust
sources: John Mordechai Gottman (1993). What Predicts Divorce?. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL1982055W

name: Name-Calling Disguised as Humor
short_definition: Putting an insult or demeaning label inside a joke, so that if you object, you can be accused of overreacting.
also_called: Sarcasm as Weapon; Humor as Weapon; disparagement humour; just joking

name: Comparative Devaluation
short_definition: Holding a person up against someone else, again and again, in a way that always leaves them coming up short.
also_called: Averages as Benchmarks; Comparison Architecture; Comparison Weaponization; Positional Scoring; Ranking Architecture; Real-Time Visibility

name: Emotional Invalidation
short_definition: Telling someone that what they feel is wrong, silly or not allowed, instead of accepting that they feel it.

name: Shame Installation
short_definition: Treating a person's mistake as proof that something is wrong with them as a whole, so shame replaces guilt.

name: Conditional Love
short_definition: Treating a person's value as something that rises and falls with their usefulness and their willingness to comply.
also_called: Conditional Worth; Conditional Approval; Love as Performance Metric; Struggle Prohibition

name: Accountability Evasion via Diagnosis / Trash-Can Diagnosis
short_definition: Using a mental-health label about someone as an insult, a verdict, or a way to treat their limits and reactions as symptoms.
also_called: Identity Diminishment via Pathologizing; Accountability Evasion via Diagnosis; Trash-Can Diagnosis; Diagnostic Deflection

name: Baiting
short_definition: Provoking someone into an angry or upset reaction, then pointing to that reaction as the real problem.

name: Performative Public Affection / Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
short_definition: Showing one warm, admired face to the world and another harsh one to a particular person. Nobody else sees how that person is treated.
also_called: Performative Public Affection; Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde; Charm Offensive; Dr. Jekyll / Mr. Hyde; Public Praise / Private Punishment

name: Ambient Abuse / Atmosphere Control
short_definition: A steady climate of tension, criticism and unpredictability. No single moment looks serious, but the whole leaves a person worn down.

name: Parentification
short_definition: A child or partner is put in the permanent role of caring for an adult's feelings, practical needs and crises, at the cost of their own development.

name: Objectification
short_definition: Treating a person as a tool, a body or a source of output, so that only what they supply seems to count about them.
sources: Fredrickson and Roberts (1997). Objectification Theory: Toward Understanding Women's Lived Experiences and Mental Health Risks. Psychology of Women Quarterly. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1471-6402.1997.tb00108.x

name: Dehumanization
short_definition: Dehumanization reduces a person to a label, a number or a problem, so decisions about them leave no room for their point of view.
sources: Bandura (1999). Moral Disengagement in the Perpetration of Inhumanities. Personality and Social Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr0303_3; Haslam (2006). Dehumanization: An Integrative Review. Personality and Social Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr1003_4

name: Toxic Positivity / Weaponized Optimism
short_definition: Toxic positivity insists on cheer in answer to real pain or a real complaint, so the feeling becomes the problem and its cause goes unexamined.

name: Public Exposure
short_definition: Someone embarrasses or puts down a person in front of others, or puts private matters on show, so the audience adds to the sting.
also_called: Public Humiliation; Public Identification; Public Shaming

name: Emotional Contamination
short_definition: Ruining positive states through sudden intrusion.

name: "You've Changed"
short_definition: Your growth, new views or new limits are described as losing your true self, so changing feels like betraying the people around you.

name: Exoticization
short_definition: A culture or identity is shown only as costume, festival or novelty, never as ordinary, present and complex.

name: Concern Trolling / Shame-as-Governance
short_definition: Voicing worry for someone's wellbeing as cover for telling them what to do, so that refusing the advice looks like harming themselves.
also_called: Shame-as-Governance Disguised as Advice; Concern Trolling; Concern Masking; Shame-as-Governance

name: Guilt-Tripping
short_definition: Using guilt about past help, sacrifice or hurt feelings to make saying no feel like a moral failing.
also_called: Obligation Hooks; Confirmshaming; Guilt Induction; Guilt Installation
sources: Baumeister et al. (1994). Guilt: An interpersonal approach. Psychological Bulletin. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.115.2.243

name: Emotional Blackmail
short_definition: Making love, closeness or the relationship itself depend on doing what someone wants, so that saying no feels like risking the bond.
also_called: Conditional Love; Conditional Safety; Emotional Blackmail via Implicit Consequence; Revocation Threat
sources: Susan Forward (1996). Emotional Blackmail. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL1929398W

name: Emotional Blackmail via Self-Harm Threats
short_definition: Someone says they will hurt or kill themselves if the other person leaves or refuses, tying that person's decision to whether the speaker lives.

name: Martyrdom Display
short_definition: Pointing out one's own unrewarded effort and sacrifice so that the other person feels in debt and unable to say no.

name: Duty Scripts
short_definition: Someone uses a role like daughter, son or parent as a rule nobody can argue with, so refusing sounds like failing at the role.

name: Demand for Gratitude
short_definition: Expecting thanks on demand, in the right words or amount, as the price of help. The generosity ends up with conditions attached.

name: Favor Debt
short_definition: Citing past gifts, money or support as the reason someone must agree to a present request. Past kindness is then treated like a signed contract.
also_called: Emotional Debt Accumulation; Obligation Layering; Reciprocity Activation

name: Withholding / Silent Treatment
short_definition: Withholding all communication, warmth or answers from someone, with no stated end. It lasts until they apologize or give in to what the other person wants.
also_called: Stonewalling; Withholding; Silent Treatment; Attention Starvation; Emotional Withholding; Love Withdrawal; Punishment by Withdrawal; icing someone out
sources: Williams (2007). Ostracism. Annual Review of Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.psych.58.110405.085641

name: Intimidation
short_definition: Using a hint or open warning of unwelcome consequences to push someone toward giving in or staying quiet.
also_called: Nonverbal Dominance; Spatial Invasion; Form Intimidation; Implied Threat; Postural Dominance; Threats of Harm; Withdrawal Pressure

name: Forced Teaming
short_definition: Declaring a shared 'we' that the other person never agreed to, so a separate choice starts to look like betrayal.
sources: Gavin de Becker (1997). The Gift of Fear. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL3355180W

name: "We're Family" Erasure
short_definition: Using family loyalty to make fairness, limits and the right to say no seem not to apply between relatives.

name: Ultimatums
short_definition: Demanding that someone pick one of two outcomes right away, with a loss attached to the option the speaker does not want.

name: Manufactured Urgency
short_definition: Someone pushes for a decision right now, often with an invented or inflated deadline or emergency, so you have no time to think or ask anyone.
also_called: Crisis Manufacturing; Pressure to Sign; Urgency Manufacturing; Commitment Before Verification; Compressed Window
part_of_patterns: Pig Butchering (Long-Con Digital Fraud); Dark Patterns (AI-Adaptive)

name: False Dilemma
short_definition: Saying there are only two possible answers when more exist, so the person feels pushed toward one.
also_called: Binary Choice Construction; false dichotomy; either/or fallacy

name: Sunk Cost Exploitation
short_definition: Pointing to the time, money or effort already spent as a reason you cannot stop, change course or leave now.
also_called: sunk cost fallacy; escalation of commitment
sources: Arkes and Blumer (1985). The psychology of sunk cost. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes. https://doi.org/10.1016/0749-5978(85)90049-4

name: Loyalty Binds
short_definition: Defining loyalty as obedience and silence, so that disagreeing, asking questions or telling outsiders counts as betrayal.

name: Sexual Coercion
short_definition: Using pressure, guilt, obligation or implied consequences to push someone into sexual activity without their free consent.

name: Reverse Psychology
short_definition: Arguing against the outcome you actually want, so that the other person's wish to resist or prove you wrong carries them to it.

name: Extinction Bursts
short_definition: A sudden, sharper surge of a pressure tactic right after it stops working, as the person tries harder to get the old result back.

name: Ambient Sexual Threat
short_definition: A sexually charged or menacing atmosphere around a person, kept alive by repeated small signals. The person stays on guard with nothing definite to report.

name: Obligation Contracts
short_definition: Holding someone to rules or debts they never agreed to and were never told about, then punishing or shaming them when they fall short.

name: "Sacred Duty" Manipulation / Mission Framing
short_definition: Presenting an ordinary request as a spiritual, moral or ancestral duty, so that saying no is treated as a sin or a betrayal.
also_called: "Sacred Duty" Manipulation; Mission Declaration; Mission Framing; Spiritual Abuse/Sacred Manipulation; Spiritual Coercion

name: Overcorrection Demands
short_definition: Overcorrection demands ask for a far larger apology, payment or gesture than a small lapse needs, so repair follows their terms, not the harm.

name: Moral Framing
short_definition: Answering someone's boundary, objection or criticism with a judgment of their character, such as selfish or disloyal, instead of with the thing they raised.

name: Negative Reinforcement Traps
short_definition: A cycle where coldness, criticism or withdrawal stays until someone gives in and then lifts at once, so giving in starts to bring relief.

name: Blackmail / Leverage Exploitation
short_definition: Holding private or damaging information, true or not, over someone to force compliance or silence, under a stated or implied threat of exposure.

name: Moral Outrage as Weapon
short_definition: Answering a disagreement with intense moral anger far out of proportion, so that questioning it looks like siding with wrongdoing.

name: Emotional Hostage-Taking
short_definition: Linking your own mood to another person's answer so openly that they feel responsible for keeping you okay.

name: Obligation Hooks
short_definition: Handing someone a secret, a sacrifice or a rule they never agreed to, then treating their loyalty as a debt they must pay.

name: Loan-Sharking Gifts
short_definition: Giving gifts, favors or help in a way that leaves the receiver in debt, so the giving can be used to press a later request.
also_called: Weaponized Generosity; Free Adoption; Gift Economy
sources: Gavin de Becker (1997). The Gift of Fear. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL3355180W

name: Guilt Legacy
short_definition: Treating a family sacrifice or an ancestor's hardship from before you were born as a debt you repay by doing what is asked.

name: Manufactured Scarcity
short_definition: Claiming that a chance, a person or a deal is about to disappear, so that fear of losing it replaces careful thought.

name: Forced Forgiveness / Weaponized Forgiveness
short_definition: Someone presses a person to forgive or move on before the harm has been acknowledged or made right, demanding forgiveness in place of repair.

name: Rage as Regulation
short_definition: Explosive anger that reliably ends a disagreement, whatever lies behind it, because the people nearby learn to give way.

name: Commitment Traps / Foot-in-the-Door
short_definition: Winning a small yes first, then using it to secure a larger one, so each agreement makes the next harder to refuse.
also_called: Graduated Compliance; Commitment Traps; Foot-in-the-Door; Escalation Testing; Gradual Escalation
sources: Freedman and Fraser (1966). Compliance without pressure: The foot-in-the-door technique. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0023552

name: Door-in-the-Face
short_definition: Making a big request that is likely to be refused so that the smaller request that follows seems modest and hard to turn down.
sources: Cialdini et al. (1975). Reciprocal concessions procedure for inducing compliance: The door-in-the-face technique. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0076284

name: Anchoring
short_definition: Putting forward a first number, price or claim that then shapes how every later figure and offer is judged.
sources: Tversky and Kahneman (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases Biases in judgments reveal some heuristics of thinking under uncertainty. Science. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.185.4157.1124

name: Cognitive Overload
short_definition: Burying someone in more information, steps or demands than they can take in, so they cannot judge a decision clearly.
also_called: Complexity Saturation; Complexity Shield; Dilution Disguise; Drip Pricing; Fee Diffusion; Financial Obfuscation; Overcomplication; Sneaking; Strategic Confusion; Structural Layering; Waterfall Opacity

name: Weaponized Generosity in Public
short_definition: Grand gestures witnessed by others to build reputation and create invisible obligation.

name: Vulnerability Weaponization
short_definition: Using shared fears or wounds as leverage.

name: Shared Secret Binding
short_definition: Creating complicity that makes leaving feel like betrayal.

name: Grooming Through Praise
short_definition: Selectively praising behaviors that serve the manipulator.

name: Anchoring to Peak Moments
short_definition: Referencing past highs to maintain present attachment.

name: Loyalty Testing
short_definition: Creating scenarios to test allegiance, then punishing failure.

name: Crisis Bonding
short_definition: Manufacturing or escalating crises to bond through shared urgency.

name: Bait Disclosure
short_definition: Pretending to reveal information to draw the target in, then weaponizing their reaction.

name: Authority Worship
short_definition: Rank, title or position is presented as beyond question, so deferring feels like a virtue and asking why feels like disrespect.

name: Reputation Braiding
short_definition: Your name is tied in public to the other party early, before any concern exists, so later criticism of them would damage you too.

name: That's-Not-All
short_definition: Before you can answer an offer, extras are added or the price is lowered, so you decide on the sweetened version without time to weigh the original.
sources: Burger (1986). Increasing compliance by improving the deal: The that's-not-all technique. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.51.2.277

name: Disrupt-Then-Reframe
short_definition: An odd or confusing phrase briefly throws you off, and a reassuring reframe arrives in the same breath, so you accept the framing before you have regrouped.
sources: Davis and Knowles (1999). A disrupt-then-reframe technique of social influence. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.76.2.192

name: Legitimizing Paltry Contributions
short_definition: A request is framed so that even the smallest contribution counts ("even a little helps"), which makes saying no at all feel unreasonable.
sources: Cialdini and Schroeder (1976). Increasing compliance by legitimizing paltry contributions: When even a penny helps. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.34.4.599

name: Phobia Indoctrination / Catastrophizing
short_definition: Intense, out-of-proportion dread attached to actions like leaving, disagreeing or trusting outsiders, until avoiding them is a bodily reflex and not a reasoned choice.

name: Controlled Opposition
short_definition: A protest group, critic or movement secretly funded, steered or shaped by the power it seems to oppose, so dissent goes somewhere harmless.

name: Echo Chamber Construction
short_definition: Arranging what another person reads, hears and talks about so they mostly meet one view and see every other source as unreliable.

name: Information Laundering
short_definition: Passing a false or unverified claim through a series of apparently credible sources until it looks like established fact and its origin can no longer be seen.

name: Humiliation Rituals
short_definition: A formal routine of shaming people in front of others, presented as initiation or growth, where the pain is treated as proof it works.

name: Manufactured Consent
short_definition: Steering what the public sees and hears so that agreement with a decision looks like free choice when it was guided.
also_called: Consent Fabrication; Democratic Validation; Mutual Agreement Fabrication; Silence Harvesting

name: Astroturfing / Sock Puppets
short_definition: Making a campaign look like spontaneous public support when it is staged, funded or run by a hidden sponsor.
also_called: Sock Puppets; Synthetic Persona Networks; Astroturfing; fake grassroots

name: False Flag Operations
short_definition: Arranging an event to look like another group's work, so a response seems justified or the blamed party is harmed.

name: Agent of Influence Operations
short_definition: A public figure, such as a journalist, academic, politician or executive, who is secretly guided by an outside party while seeming to speak independently.

name: Strategic Leaking
short_definition: Releasing sensitive information through channels that look unauthorized, so a planned disclosure looks like a secret that got out.

name: Cyber Manipulation Operations (CMOs)
short_definition: Quietly changing, inventing or deleting data inside a system, so people make decisions based on records they believe are real.

name: Mystical Manipulation
short_definition: Staging events that look spontaneous or divine, like visions, healings or signs, to persuade members that a leader holds special spiritual authority.
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Sacred Science
short_definition: Treating the group's doctrine as beyond question, so a doubt is read as a flaw in the doubter and the claim goes unexamined.
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Doctrine Over Person
short_definition: Teaching members that if their own experience, memory or conscience contradicts the group's doctrine, then the experience, and not the doctrine, must be wrong.
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Dispensing of Existence
short_definition: A group's doctrine sorts people by who deserves to exist or counts as fully human, which makes harm to outsiders, critics and former members seem justified.
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Charismatic Authority Dependence
short_definition: Making a single leader the only trusted source of truth, meaning and safety, so that winning the leader's approval becomes a member's deepest need.

name: Forced Confession / Self-Criticism Rituals
short_definition: Required, repeated sharing of faults, doubts or past wrongs with the group, which brings shame and gives the group material it can hold over people.
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Isolation
short_definition: Steadily cutting a person off from friends, family and other outside support, until only one relationship is left.
sources: Evan Stark (2007). Coercive Control. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL2982769W

name: Location Tracking
short_definition: Requiring a person to keep their live location visible. Any gap in it is treated as a problem to be explained.
sources: Freed et al. (2018). “A Stalker's Paradise” How Intimate Partner Abusers Exploit Technology. Proceedings of the 2018 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3174241

name: Infantilization
short_definition: Treating a capable adult as if they cannot manage their own money, tasks or decisions, and taking those over.

name: "I Know Best" Paternalism / Velvet Glove Control
short_definition: Overriding another adult's choices in the name of what is good for them, and expecting them to be grateful.
also_called: Velvet Glove Control; "I Know Best" Paternalism; Using Privilege

name: Punishment of Boundaries
short_definition: When someone sets a limit, the other person answers with a penalty, such as coldness, withdrawn help or a taken-away privilege. Saying no starts to feel costly.

name: Response-Time Policing
short_definition: Treating the time taken to answer a message as a failing that must be explained, so you feel permanently on call.

name: Omnipresence / Demonstrating Omnipotence
short_definition: Showing off how much someone knows, controls or can reach in your life, until trying to act independently starts to look pointless.

name: Interrogation
short_definition: Demanding that someone explain, justify or defend themselves on command. The demander acts as if an answer is owed, whether or not the person wants to give one.

name: Financial Control
short_definition: Limiting what someone can reach, see or earn, or using money and assets to pressure them, so they depend on one person.
also_called: Financial Enmeshment; Economic Abuse; Economic Coercion; Financial Isolation
sources: Adams et al. (2008). Development of the Scale of Economic Abuse. Violence Against Women. https://doi.org/10.1177/1077801208315529; Postmus et al. (2012). Understanding Economic Abuse in the Lives of Survivors. Journal of Interpersonal Violence. https://doi.org/10.1177/0886260511421669

name: Financial Dependence by Design
short_definition: Setting up money, work and account access so that one person cannot manage alone, no matter how either person feels about the relationship.

name: Maternal Gatekeeping
short_definition: A mother repeatedly corrects, redoes or limits the other parent's or caregiver's care of a child, until that person loses confidence and steps back.
sources: Allen and Hawkins (1999). Maternal Gatekeeping: Mothers' Beliefs and Behaviors That Inhibit Greater Father Involvement in Family Work. Journal of Marriage and the Family. https://doi.org/10.2307/353894

name: Ritualized Exhaustion
short_definition: A relentless run of schedules, demands and lost sleep that keeps a person too depleted to think clearly, weigh options or push back.

name: Resource Sabotage / Sabotaging Success
short_definition: Taking away the tools, information, money or help someone needs, and calling the failure proof they are not up to it.
also_called: Sabotaging Success; Resource Sabotage; Resource Consequence

name: Reproductive Coercion
short_definition: Pressuring or penalizing someone over whether, when or how to have children, using money, work, family standing or withdrawal of support.
sources: Miller et al. (2010). Pregnancy coercion, intimate partner violence and unintended pregnancy. Contraception. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.contraception.2009.12.004

name: Moving-in-Silence
short_definition: Settling a big matter that changes someone else's life without telling or asking them, so they hear about it only when it is finished.

name: Smart-Home Coercion
short_definition: Using connected home devices like locks, cameras, thermostats and speakers to watch, unsettle or control another person at home.

name: Health Sabotage
short_definition: Interfering with someone's medicine, sleep, food, exercise or medical care in ways that make them weaker and more dependent.

name: Legal Abuse
short_definition: Repeatedly using court filings, motions and hearings after a separation to drain the other person's money, time and stability.
also_called: Legal Abuse (Post-Separation); SLAPP; Silencing Litigation; paper abuse; litigation abuse; vexatious litigation
sources: Miller and Smolter (2011). “Paper Abuse”: When All Else Fails, Batterers Use Procedural Stalking. Violence Against Women. https://doi.org/10.1177/1077801211407290; Gutowski and Goodman (2022). Coercive Control in the Courtroom: the Legal Abuse Scale (LAS). Journal of Family Violence. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10896-022-00408-3; Spearman et al. (2022). Post‐separation abuse: A concept analysis. Journal of Advanced Nursing. https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.15310

name: Device Access Demands
short_definition: Insisting on passwords, an unlocked phone or account logins as proof of trust, so that having a private space is read as hiding something.
sources: Freed et al. (2018). “A Stalker's Paradise” How Intimate Partner Abusers Exploit Technology. Proceedings of the 2018 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3174241

name: Enforcing Trivial Demands
short_definition: Insisting on exact compliance with small, pointless-looking rules, treated far more seriously than the stakes deserve, until going along becomes routine.

name: Boundary Testing
short_definition: Someone crosses a stated or implied limit in small steps, and each step that goes unchallenged is followed by a slightly bigger one.

name: Forced Dependency
short_definition: One person sets up a relationship or setting so the other cannot manage without their ongoing help, and then keeps it that way.
also_called: Dependency Engineering; Dependency Installation; Device Dependency; Ecosystem Embedding

name: Golden Bars
short_definition: Someone offers real comfort, money or status that comes with unspoken conditions, so leaving or disagreeing means losing a good life.

name: Time Theft
short_definition: Someone repeatedly spends another person's time carelessly, through lateness, waiting and canceled plans, as if those hours were worth less than their own.

name: Choice Restriction
short_definition: Someone closes off or hides your realistic options one by one, until a single outcome looks like the only sensible choice.
also_called: Choice Architecture Manipulation; Bounded Choice; Reflexive Control; Coercive Framing; Institutional Adoption; Token Autonomy; Token Autonomy / Coercive Framing

name: Financial Enmeshment
short_definition: Tangling finances to make separation catastrophic.

name: Strategic Chaos / Crisis Manufacturing
short_definition: Constant emergencies preventing strategic thinking.

name: Time Control
short_definition: Dictating how every hour is spent to prevent autonomous thought.

name: Sleep Deprivation
short_definition: Disrupting rest to reduce cognitive and emotional resistance.

name: Mobility Control
short_definition: Restricting physical movement to enforce submission.

name: Body Autonomy Violations
short_definition: Controlling the physical body under institutional justification.

name: Role Assignment
short_definition: Assigning fixed identities that dictate expectation and treatment.
also_called: Identification as Identity Assignment; Identity Narrowing; Role Confinement

name: Children as Leverage
short_definition: Using children's wellbeing as a tool of control over adults.
sources: Spearman et al. (2022). Post‐separation abuse: A concept analysis. Journal of Advanced Nursing. https://doi.org/10.1111/jan.15310

name: Performance Monitoring
short_definition: Constant evaluation that installs hypervigilance.

name: Controlled Communication
short_definition: Dictating how, when, and whether you may speak.
also_called: Communication Chain Restriction; Constraining Verbal Expression; Vocal Regulation

name: Fear Installation
short_definition: Creating persistent dread through unpredictable consequences.

name: Institutional Capture
short_definition: Influence is gained over the bodies meant to provide oversight, or outside structures are lined up to enforce, so the place you would turn to for help is already on their side.
sources: Stigler (1971). The Theory of Economic Regulation. The Bell Journal of Economics and Management Science. https://doi.org/10.2307/3003160

name: Arbitrary Authority
short_definition: Decisions follow no stated rule, so nothing you do reliably changes the outcome.

name: Collective Punishment
short_definition: A whole group is punished for something one person did, or for something no one is named for, so the group turns its pressure inward.
also_called: Collective Consequence; Incident Identification Without Individual Accountability

name: Strategic Timing
short_definition: Damaging information or sudden pressure arrives just before an important moment, leaving no time to check or respond.

name: Harm to Pets or Property
short_definition: Belongings are destroyed, or a pet is harmed or threatened, as a warning of what could happen next. (Treat as a safety risk: contact local emergency or domestic violence services.).
sources: Ascione (1997). Battered Women's Reports of Their Partners' and Their Children's Cruelty to Animals. Journal of Emotional Abuse. https://doi.org/10.1300/J135v01n01_06

name: Coerced Debt
short_definition: Loans, credit or bills are taken out in your name, or you are pressured into them, without real consent, so you carry debt for someone else's control.

name: Debt Bondage
short_definition: Fees for travel, housing, training or recruitment are charged against future earnings and keep growing, so you must keep working to pay a debt that never clears.

name: Document Confiscation
short_definition: Passports, identity papers, visas or certificates are taken "for safekeeping", so leaving, travelling or proving who you are depends on someone else.

name: Status Threats
short_definition: Your visa, residency, enrollment or legal status is used as a threat: comply, or you or your family could be reported, removed or deported. (Route to independent legal advice and support services.).

name: Enmeshment
short_definition: The line between two people's feelings, choices and identities is dissolved, so your moods, decisions and successes are treated as belonging to someone else. (A family-systems concept.).

name: Legal / Administrative Threats
short_definition: Raising the police, lawyers, HR, courts or other authorities as pressure in a personal or workplace dispute, instead of as part of a real process.

name: Confidentiality as Weapon
short_definition: Citing confidentiality rules to keep from someone the accusation, the evidence or even the source of a complaint against them. They are left unable to answer it.
also_called: Confidentiality Binding; Confidentiality Weaponization; Opacity Shield; Privacy Weaponization

name: "Polite Hostile" Environments
short_definition: A workplace or social setting that stays polite on the surface but quietly punishes anyone who speaks plainly or disagrees.

name: Process Exhaustion
short_definition: Steps, forms, meetings and re-reviews keep piling up until the person gives up worn out, and not because their matter was decided.
also_called: Paper Terrorism; Documentation Extraction; Exhaustion Yield; Form Gatekeeping; Internal Exhaustion Prerequisite; Procedural Embedding; Sludge; administrative burden
sources: Moynihan et al. (2014). Administrative Burden: Learning, Psychological, and Compliance Costs in Citizen-State Interactions. Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory. https://doi.org/10.1093/jopart/muu009

name: HR Shielding
short_definition: A workplace complaints process that, in practice, protects the organization's reputation and the accused person better than it protects the employee who reported harm.
also_called: Strategic HR Complicity; Dutiful Reporting; Firewall Function

name: Pseudo-Consultation
short_definition: Asking for opinions, feedback or comment after the decision is already made, when the input can no longer change anything.
also_called: Pre-Decision Concealment; Process Performance; Structural Dilution
sources: Arnstein (1969). A Ladder Of Citizen Participation. Journal of the American Institute of Planners. https://doi.org/10.1080/01944366908977225

name: Tokenism
short_definition: Including one person, or a small number of people, from a group as a visible gesture. They are not given the voice or authority that inclusion seems to promise.
sources: Kanter (1977). Some Effects of Proportions on Group Life: Skewed Sex Ratios and Responses to Token Women. American Journal of Sociology. https://doi.org/10.1086/226425

name: Individualization of Systemic Issues
short_definition: Calling a problem of workload, staffing or structure a personal weakness, and expecting the individual to fix it.

name: Diffusion of Responsibility
short_definition: A decision or harm gets spread across so many people and steps that no one can be found who is answerable for it.
also_called: "Just Following Orders"; Accountability Diffusion; Accountability Fragmentation; Authority Displacement; Jurisdictional Displacement; Responsibility Displacement
sources: Darley and Latane (1968). Bystander intervention in emergencies: Diffusion of responsibility. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0025589

name: Performative Allyship / False Solidarity
short_definition: Public support for a cause or group that private actions and choices do not match, so it earns trust it has not backed up.

name: Administrative Escalation
short_definition: Turning a small, informal concern into a formal complaint, report or legal step that is far heavier than what actually happened.
also_called: PIP Weaponization; Intervention Cascade; Professional Degradation

name: Credit Laundering
short_definition: Passing someone's idea or work along through several people, each rewording it a little, until no one can trace it back to the person.

name: Credit Theft
short_definition: Someone presents another person's work, idea or effort as their own, or lets the credit drift away from the person who made it.

name: Gatekeeping
short_definition: Controlling who can reach certain people, information, resources or opportunities, so some people must ask permission while others get in without asking.
also_called: Access Control; Access Gatekeeping; Financial Filtration; ID Gatekeeping; Institutional Verification Monopoly; Legal Gatekeeping; Standardized Assessment Gatekeeping

name: Weaponized Inclusion / Strategic Containment
short_definition: Placing someone in a group or process where they stay visible but have little real influence, so being included replaces acting independently.
also_called: Critique Absorption; Dissent Absorption; Inclusion Capture; co-optation

name: "Managed Out" Through Exhaustion
short_definition: Slowly removing a person's meaningful work, visibility and belonging until their leaving looks like a free choice on paper.
also_called: Discard by Degradation; Self-Exile Completion; constructive dismissal; quiet firing

name: Willful Blindness as Complicity
short_definition: Not looking into, acknowledging or acting on wrongdoing there is good reason to suspect, so that 'I didn't know' can be said later.
also_called: Active Danger Preservation; Successor Enablement; Systemic Neglect Documentation

name: Silence as Policy
short_definition: Building a workplace culture in which people learn that speaking up brings punishment and staying quiet brings safety.
also_called: Organizational Silence Engineering; Challenge Suppression; Permanent Silencing; organisational silence; code of silence
sources: Morrison and Milliken (2000). Organizational Silence: A Barrier to Change and Development in a Pluralistic World. The Academy of Management Review. https://doi.org/10.5465/amr.2000.3707697

name: Performance Framework Manipulation
short_definition: Designing ratings, targets and reviews so that agreement and loyalty are rewarded, and skill, dissent and ethical objection are marked down.

name: Micromanagement
short_definition: Software that assigns tasks, tracks output and makes decisions about workers' hours, pay or jobs, with little human review.
also_called: Algorithmic Management; Autonomy Displacement; Pattern Recognition as Evaluation; Teacher Displacement

name: Impossible Metrics
short_definition: Giving someone a task or standard they are unlikely to meet with the means given, then treating the miss as proof they are inadequate.
also_called: Setting Up to Fail; Expectation Inflation; Impossible Standards; Perfectionism Installation

name: False Reports
short_definition: Making a formal complaint to an employer, school, agency or police that the filer knows is untrue, so the accused answers for something that never happened.

name: Paper-Trail Traps
short_definition: Creating or shaping written records, like write-ups, emails and notes, to build a one-sided case against someone who does not know it is happening.
also_called: Asymmetric Curation; Institutional Citation; Pattern Seeding; Preemptive Documentation; Selective Record-Keeping; Weaponized Documentation

name: Performative Reception
short_definition: A concern is received with warmth, speed and sympathy, but nothing that follows changes what happened.
also_called: Institutional Intake Performance; Procedural Legitimation; Responsive Performance; Responsive Velocity; Sympathetic Intake

name: Deniable Authorization
short_definition: Permission is given only in conversation or by hint, never in writing, so it can later be denied.

name: Cultural Penalty
short_definition: Speech, work or knowledge that differs from one dominant style is marked as wrong or lesser, whatever its substance.
also_called: Knowledge Hierarchy Enforcement; Training Data Bias

name: Experience Erasure
short_definition: Real experience, skill or history is declared not to count because it lacks the system's own credential, format or record.
sources: Fricker (2007). Epistemic Injustice Power and the Ethics of Knowing. Oxford University PressOxford. https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198237907.001.0001

name: Stigma Marking
short_definition: A person's need, status or condition is made visible to others through separate lines, labels, colors, rooms or lists.
also_called: Architectural Stigma; Categorical Visibility; Peer Witnessing
sources: Erving Goffman (1963). Stigma. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL3282007W

name: Unwritten Rules
short_definition: Success depends on expectations nobody states, and people who did not arrive already knowing them are judged as failing.

name: Abstraction Escalation
short_definition: A question about one specific harm is answered with broad statements about values, mission or culture, so the event itself is never named.

name: Agent Erasure
short_definition: Accounts of what happened leave out who did it ("mistakes were made", "the decision was taken"), so no one is answerable.

name: Captive Expertise
short_definition: An outside expert is chosen or briefed so their findings support a decision already made, and their credentials are then used to end debate.

name: Done-Deal Framing
short_definition: A decision is announced as already final and inevitable, so objecting feels pointless before anyone has been asked.

name: Language Laundering
short_definition: Cuts, losses or harms are described in soft, technical or upbeat words, so they sound like improvements.
sources: Bandura (1999). Moral Disengagement in the Perpetration of Inhumanities. Personality and Social Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1207/s15327957pspr0303_3

name: Metric Masking
short_definition: Averages, color codes and summary figures stand in for what happened to particular people, so overall numbers look fine while specific harm disappears.
also_called: Aggregate Reporting Substitution; Decontextualized Measurement; Visual Simplification; vanity metrics
sources: Campbell (1979). Assessing the impact of planned social change. Evaluation and Program Planning. https://doi.org/10.1016/0149-7189(79)90048-X

name: Policy as Proof
short_definition: The existence of a written policy is offered as proof that a problem is handled, in place of evidence that the policy works.

name: Self-Fulfilling Prediction
short_definition: A prediction about a person shapes how they are treated, and the outcome that treatment produces is then cited as proof the prediction was right.
also_called: Confirmation Feedback Loop; Self-Fulfilling Degradation; self-fulfilling prophecy
sources: Merton (1948). The Self-Fulfilling Prophecy. The Antioch Review. https://doi.org/10.2307/4609267

name: Solution Theater
short_definition: A visible purchase, program, support service or announcement is presented as the fix, while the cause of the problem stays untouched.

name: Front-Person Exposure
short_definition: One person is made the public face of a decision many people shared, so they take the reaction alone.

name: Incident Siloing
short_definition: Each complaint is handled and closed on its own, in its own office or site, so no one is placed to see that the cases form a pattern.
also_called: Campus-Level Containment; Case Closure Protocol; Cross-Campus Blindness

name: Participation Penalty
short_definition: Taking part, asking for help or speaking up exposes a person to new risk, so staying away becomes the safer choice.

name: Managed Perception
short_definition: Controlling how the system appears to outsiders.

name: Celebration as Cover
short_definition: Overwork, self-funding or sacrifice is praised in public as dedication, so the shortage that required it is never fixed.
also_called: Celebration Capture; Celebration as Extraction Cover

name: Closed-Loop Appeals
short_definition: Challenging a decision sends you back to the same people, rules or system that made it.

name: Development Subordination
short_definition: A person's own learning, health or future is ranked below their usefulness to the system, and that ranking is presented as opportunity.

name: Initiative Churn
short_definition: New programs are launched one after another, so activity looks like progress while none runs long enough to be judged.

name: Labor Extraction
short_definition: Work, time, care or personal money beyond what was agreed or paid is expected and uncounted, often because the role has grown too big or because stopping would hurt the people you serve.
also_called: Administrative Displacement; Compassion Exploitation; Invisibility of Clinical Labor; Performance Extraction; Personal Subsidy Extraction; Ratio Exploitation; Role Inflation; Role Overload

name: Liability Reframing
short_definition: A duty to protect or repair is handed to legal or risk management and treated as exposure to limit, then declared expired, out of scope or not owed.

name: Metric-Mission Substitution
short_definition: The numbers chosen to measure a purpose quietly replace the purpose, and people are judged on the numbers.
also_called: Engagement-Learning Conflation; Metric Installation; Metric Substitution
sources: Campbell (1979). Assessing the impact of planned social change. Evaluation and Program Planning. https://doi.org/10.1016/0149-7189(79)90048-X

name: Motivation Displacement
short_definition: Points, scores and rewards replace a person's own reasons for doing something, so they stop when the reward stops.
also_called: Intrinsic Motivation Displacement; Intrinsic-Extrinsic Displacement; Joy Extinction; overjustification effect
sources: Lepper et al. (1973). Undermining children's intrinsic interest with extrinsic reward: A test of the "overjustification" hypothesis. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0035519

name: Predictive Tracking
short_definition: People are routed into tracks, groups or labels on the strength of a prediction, and the track then limits what they are offered and can become.
also_called: Automatic Sorting; Intervention Channeling; Track Solidification

name: Strategic Delay
short_definition: Responses, records or decisions are slowed until deadlines pass, evidence fades or the person gives up.
also_called: Access Delay; Recommendation Deferral; Timeline Elongation; Timeline Exploitation

name: Structural Underfunding
short_definition: The service meant to help is kept too small, too thinly staffed or too run-down to work, and its failure is treated as nobody's fault.

name: Manufactured Closure
short_definition: The matter is declared resolved or closed by the side that caused it, without the harmed person agreeing and without the harm being named.
also_called: Closure Manufacture; Quiet Resolution; Resolution Without Acknowledgment; Unilateral Resolution

name: Paid Silence
short_definition: Money, a reference, a role or another benefit is offered in exchange for not speaking about what happened.
also_called: Positive Reference Leverage; Silence Incentivization; hush money

name: Punitive Transfer
short_definition: After raising a concern, the person is moved to a different place, team, class or role, presented as routine.

name: Record Erasure
short_definition: Records, files or evidence of what happened are deleted, lost or sealed, so the event can later be denied.

name: Values-Fit Pretext
short_definition: A person's results or questions are redescribed as a mismatch with the group's values or culture, which becomes the reason they have to go.

name: Visible Impunity
short_definition: The person reported faces no visible consequence, which tells everyone watching that reporting does not work.

name: Accountability Reset
short_definition: A change of leader, name or program is treated as a fresh start, so earlier promises and failures no longer count against anyone.

name: Tone Policing
short_definition: Responding to how something was said and not what was said, so the complaint is never actually discussed.
also_called: "You're Too Emotional"; Clinical Tone Policing; Frame Assassination; tone argument

name: Minimization
short_definition: Shrinking how serious something was so that your reaction looks too big for what actually happened.
also_called: Trivializing; False Conclusion from Normal Labs; Medical Gaslighting; Effort Minimization; Gaslighting by Minimization

name: Pity Plays
short_definition: Answering a concern by showing helplessness or being the victim. The person who raised it ends up giving comfort, and the concern is dropped.
also_called: Strategic Self-Deprecation / Performed Humility; Weaponized Tears; Strategic Self-Deprecation; Strategic Vulnerability; Strategic Vulnerability / Weaponized Tears; playing the victim; self-victimisation

name: Blame-Shifting
short_definition: Placing the cause of your own action on the other person, so that your choice is described as something they did to you.

name: Whataboutism
short_definition: The reply to a complaint raises a different wrong from the other side. The original issue goes unanswered.

name: Non-Apology Apologies
short_definition: A statement that sounds like an apology but regrets your reaction or feelings, not the thing that was actually done.

name: Kafka Trapping
short_definition: Treating a person's denial of an accusation as proof of guilt, so that no answer they give could ever clear them.

name: Weaponized Therapy-Speak
short_definition: Using therapy words such as boundaries, projecting or triggered to turn someone's limits and complaints into the problem. The real issue goes unanswered.
also_called: Role Reversal via Therapy Language; Pseudo-Insight as Shutdown; Identity Diminishment via Pathologizing; Sanity Framing; Therapeutic Manipulation/Pathological Framing; Weaponized Therapy Language; therapy-speak

name: False Equivalence
short_definition: Presenting very uneven harm as equally shared fault, so that no one is left holding the larger share.
also_called: Conflict Reframing; File Equalization; Procedural Symmetry; false balance; bothsidesism

name: Weaponized Incompetence
short_definition: A pattern in which someone seems unable to do an unwanted task, so that it falls to another person for good.

name: Strategic Apathy / Weaponized Indifference
short_definition: Saying 'I don't care' or 'whatever you want' at decision points, then picking apart whatever the other person chooses.

name: Malicious Compliance
short_definition: Doing exactly what was asked, to the letter, in a way that predictably defeats the point of the request.

name: Moral Licensing / Strategic Philanthropy
short_definition: Pointing to a good character or past good deeds as a reason the present complaint does not need an answer.
also_called: Moral Licensing; Strategic Benevolence; Strategic Benevolence / Strategic Philanthropy; Strategic Philanthropy; Virtue Signaling as Shield
sources: Monin and Miller (2001). Moral credentials and the expression of prejudice. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.81.1.33

name: Competitive Victimhood
short_definition: Meeting someone's hurt with a bigger hurt of your own, so the conversation ends up about whose pain is worse.

name: Halo Effect Exploitation
short_definition: Answering a concern about someone's behavior by pointing to their achievements, talent or reputation, which have nothing to do with it.
sources: Thorndike (1920). A constant error in psychological ratings. Journal of Applied Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0071663

name: Projection
short_definition: Charging someone with a behavior or motive that the exchange shows more clearly in the person making the charge.

name: Deflection
short_definition: Steering a conversation away from the issue that was raised, so the concern never gets a direct answer.
also_called: Diverting; Rapid Topic Switching; Gaslighting by Deflection; Topic Shifting; Topic Switching

name: Apologies Without Repair
short_definition: An apology is offered but no change in behavior follows, so the same harm returns and the apology closes the matter each time.

name: Plausible Deniability
short_definition: Someone acts in ways that can always be explained as concern, policy or accident, so no single incident can be called harmful without the accuser sounding unfair.

name: Feigned Ignorance
short_definition: Someone acts as if they do not know or cannot follow something, so a responsibility is dropped or a hard conversation is put off.

name: Role Reversal Traps
short_definition: Someone calls themselves the injured party when asked about harm, so sympathy shifts away from the person actually hurt.
also_called: Victim Role Reversal; Reputational Threat Conversion; Role Reversal via Therapy Language

name: Preemptive Accusation / Complaint Weaponization
short_definition: Someone accuses another person of a fault first, often the very one they expect to hear about, so the reply sounds like a copy.

name: Counterfeit Calm
short_definition: Putting on an unbothered, composed manner so that someone's honest upset looks irrational or excessive by comparison.

name: Blame Discard
short_definition: Framing the discard as the target's fault.

name: Managed Exit
short_definition: Orchestrating the departure to maximize the system's control over the narrative.

name: Catfishing
short_definition: Building an online relationship behind a made-up identity, such as borrowed photos or an invented life story, so someone bonds with a person who does not exist.

name: AI Voice Cloning
short_definition: Software-made copies of a real person's voice, used to impersonate them in calls, messages or recordings.

name: Doxxing
short_definition: Publishing a person's private details, such as a home address or workplace, so others can find or harass them.

name: Coordinated Reporting
short_definition: Organized mass reporting of an account or post, often on false grounds, to get a platform to remove or restrict it.

name: Social Engineering
short_definition: Getting someone to hand over information, access or action by playing on their trust, urgency or habits, usually with a false story.

name: Account Control
short_definition: Taking over someone's email, social media, banking or cloud accounts, so they are watched, spoken for and cut off from their online life.
sources: Freed et al. (2018). “A Stalker's Paradise” How Intimate Partner Abusers Exploit Technology. Proceedings of the 2018 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems. https://doi.org/10.1145/3173574.3174241

name: Intimate Image Abuse
short_definition: Sharing or threatening to share private sexual images of someone without consent, including fake ones, often with a demand for money, contact or compliance.
also_called: Deepfake / AI Voice / SIM Swap / Intimate Image Abuse / Smart-Home Coercion; revenge porn; image-based sexual abuse; non-consensual intimate images
sources: McGlynn and Rackley (2017). Image-Based Sexual Abuse. Oxford Journal of Legal Studies. https://doi.org/10.1093/ojls/gqw033

name: Algorithmic Manipulation
short_definition: Using feed ranking and recommendation systems to steer what a person sees and feels, in ways they cannot inspect or switch off.

name: Context Poisoning
short_definition: Planting misleading or tampered material in shared information sources, or in AI training data, so that later readers and tools inherit the error.

name: Parasocial Manipulation Engineering
short_definition: Building a one-sided feeling of friendship or closeness with an audience, then using it to draw out loyalty, money, personal information or compliance.
sources: Horton and Richard Wohl (1956). Mass Communication and Para-Social Interaction Observations on Intimacy at a Distance. Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1080/00332747.1956.11023049

name: Immersive Manipulation (VR/AR)
short_definition: Using virtual or augmented reality experiences to make staged scenarios seem real enough to shape someone's fears, beliefs or attachments.

name: Biometric Exploitation
short_definition: Reading someone's face, voice or body signals in real time, often without clear knowledge, to time or tune an attempt to influence them.

name: Algorithmic Targeting of Vulnerable Populations
short_definition: Finding people in a weak moment through their data, then targeting them with exploitative offers, scams or harmful content.

name: Buried Consent
short_definition: Agreement is collected through long, vague or scattered terms that no ordinary person can realistically read, then treated as full and informed consent.
also_called: Buried Consent Disclosure; Consent Theater; Disaggregated Consent; Standard-Term Camouflage

name: Gamified Compulsion
short_definition: Streaks, badges, levels and progress bars make stopping feel like losing something already earned.

name: Forced Continuity
short_definition: A free or low-cost start turns into ongoing payment or commitment without a clear moment where you choose to continue.

name: Persistent Nagging
short_definition: The same request or prompt keeps coming back, with no way to make it stop, until giving in is easier than saying no again.

name: Reputation Hijacking
short_definition: Someone takes control of how you are presented in public, speaking for you or reshaping your image, so your own account no longer reaches people first.

name: Black-Box Decisions
short_definition: Consequential decisions come from a system whose workings cannot be seen, explained or meaningfully questioned.
also_called: High-Stakes Consequence; Invisibility of the Mechanism
sources: Pasquale (2015). The Black Box Society The Secret Algorithms That Control Money and Information. Harvard University Press. https://doi.org/10.4159/harvard.9780674736061

name: Data Harvesting
short_definition: Detailed information about behavior, location, feelings or performance is collected continuously and built into a profile, far beyond what the service needs.
also_called: Ambient Data Collection; Data Accumulation; Data Point Extraction; Profile Construction

name: Data Onward Sharing
short_definition: Information collected for one purpose is passed, sold or shown to others, often described as anonymized, without the person's real knowledge.
also_called: De-identification Laundering; Non-Consensual Distribution; Secondary Market Exploitation

name: Uncorrected Record
short_definition: The accusation is public, loud and lasting, while any correction is quiet or missing, so the first version stays.

name: Swatting
short_definition: A false emergency report brings an armed or emergency response to someone's home or school, using the authorities as a weapon. (Treat as an emergency safety risk.).

name: Manufactured Intimacy
short_definition: Creating deep closeness fast, through early confessions and painful sharing, before the two people have any shared history to support it.
part_of_patterns: Honey Trapping; Pig Butchering (Long-Con Digital Fraud)

name: Love Bombing
short_definition: Flooding someone with intense affection, praise and attention very early. The pace outruns how well the two people actually know each other.

name: Exclusive Meaning
short_definition: Claiming that only this one person truly understands you. Gradually, everyone else in your life seems less worthy of your trust.

name: Hoovering / Relief Bait
short_definition: Reaching out to draw someone back into a relationship after they have pulled away or ended it. This often comes with promises that things will change.
also_called: Relief Bait; Hoovering; Hoovering (Post-Discard); Hoovering (Replacement Phase); Periodic Reinforcement of the Ideal; Zombieing

name: Future Faking
short_definition: Making vivid promises about a better future together that keep you invested in the present. The promised things never seem to arrive.

name: Identity Hooking
short_definition: Saying that someone's identity, skills or successes belong to you, so that standing apart from you means giving up the self they have built.

name: Pedestal Ploy / The Exception Script
short_definition: Telling you that you are uniquely different from everyone around you. Keeping that special status then depends on staying close to the speaker.
also_called: Pedestal Ploy; The Exception Script; Social Elevation; The Exception Script (Recycled)

name: Intermittent Reinforcement / Push-Pull
short_definition: A repeating cycle of warmth and distance that leaves the other person working to get back to the warm stretch.
also_called: Intermittent Reinforcement; Push-Pull; Emotional Bait-and-Switch; Intermittent Availability; Occasional Indulgences; Proximity Control; Push-Pull / Rubberbanding; Push-Pull Cycling; Variable Ratio Reinforcement; Variable Reward Scheduling
sources: Charles B. Ferster (1957). Schedules of Reinforcement. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL6445502W

name: Bread-crumbing
short_definition: Sending just enough occasional attention to keep someone hopeful and available, while the contact never turns into real plans or commitment.
also_called: Benching; Breadcrumbing; Cushioning; Hope as a Leash; stringing someone along

name: Ghosting as Control
short_definition: Cutting off all contact with no explanation and then returning later, leaving the other person with questions they cannot settle.
sources: LeFebvre et al. (2019). Ghosting in Emerging Adults’ Romantic Relationships: The Digital Dissolution Disappearance Strategy. Imagination, Cognition and Personality. https://doi.org/10.1177/0276236618820519

name: Premature Exclusivity
short_definition: Pushing someone to commit exclusively and seriously before they have had time to know you well enough to choose freely.

name: Confirmation Bias Exploitation
short_definition: Supplying enough good moments that your own habit of favoring the kinder reading does the work of discounting the harm.
sources: Nickerson (1998). Confirmation Bias: A Ubiquitous Phenomenon in Many Guises. Review of General Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/1089-2680.2.2.175

name: Manufactured Destiny
short_definition: Presenting a relationship as fated or cosmically arranged, so that doubting it, slowing it down or leaving it is treated as going against destiny.

name: Mirroring-on-Demand
short_definition: Quickly copying your interests, opinions and way of speaking so you feel unusually understood, whether or not the match is real.

name: The Rescue Hook
short_definition: Showing a need that seems helpless, so you take over tasks or feelings unasked and your effort is treated as devotion.

name: Emotional Parasitism
short_definition: A steady one-way arrangement where one person's feelings get the attention and care, and the other is drained with little given back.

name: Splitting
short_definition: Seeing a person or group as all good or all bad, with no middle ground, and flipping that view suddenly after a minor event.

name: Emotional Flooding
short_definition: Pouring on emotion so fast and so hard that the other person cannot think, until speed and intensity get mistaken for closeness.

name: Premature Vulnerability / Trauma Dumping
short_definition: Deep disclosures too early to create obligation and recruit caretaking.

name: Premature Trust Extraction
short_definition: Pressuring the target to share before earning the right to hold it.

name: Identity Auditing
short_definition: Mapping the target's vulnerabilities for strategic use.

name: Rescuer Positioning
short_definition: Presenting as the answer to the target's confusion or fear.

name: Pacing and Leading
short_definition: First matching the target's rhythm, then shifting it toward dependency.

name: Target Selection
short_definition: One person is singled out for special attention because they look most isolated, most eager or most useful, and the attention feels like being chosen.

name: Gatekeeper Grooming
short_definition: The people around a target, such as parents, colleagues or an institution, are won over first, so that later access goes unquestioned and concerns are not believed.

name: Pocketing
short_definition: You are kept apart from the other person's friends, family and public life, so the relationship exists only in private, with no witnesses. (Informal term from dating culture; no peer-reviewed research was found.).

name: Sudden Devaluation
short_definition: An abrupt shift from investment to disposal.

name: Replacement Display
short_definition: Publicly showcasing your replacement to signal your disposability.

name: Orbiting
short_definition: Watching from a distance to maintain psychological presence after discard.

name: DARVO
short_definition: A three-part reply to being confronted: deny it happened, attack the person raising it, then claim to be the one who was wronged.
made_of: Countering; Credibility Theft; Role Reversal Traps
