sources: Freyd (1997). Violations of Power, Adaptive Blindness and Betrayal Trauma Theory. Feminism & Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1177/0959353597071004; Harsey et al. (2017). Perpetrator Responses to Victim Confrontation: DARVO and Victim Self-Blame. Journal of Aggression, Maltreatment & Trauma. https://doi.org/10.1080/10926771.2017.1320777

name: Computational Propaganda
short_definition: Using bots, fake accounts and automated tools to flood public talk with political messages posing as real opinion, at a scale no crowd could match.
made_of: Astroturfing / Sock Puppets; Algorithmic Manipulation
sources: Woolley and Howard (2018). Computational Propaganda. Oxford Scholarship Online. https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780190931407.001.0001

name: Demand for Purity
short_definition: Setting a standard of moral perfection that no one can meet, which leaves members ashamed and looking only to the group for forgiveness.
made_of: Impossible Metrics; Splitting
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Honey Trapping
short_definition: Using a romantic or sexual relationship as cover for an intelligence aim, like getting secrets, recruiting someone, or collecting material for later pressure.
made_of: Manufactured Intimacy; Shared Secret Binding; Blackmail / Leverage Exploitation

name: Milieu Control
short_definition: A group's tight control over what members can read, hear and discuss and whom they see, so the group becomes their only source of information.
made_of: Information Control; Isolation; Controlled Communication
sources: Robert Jay Lifton (1961). Thought Reform and the Psychology of Totalism. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL15241904W

name: Strategic Deception (Denial & Deception / D&D)
short_definition: Organized efforts by a state or institution to hide what is real and show something false, so an opponent plans against a mistaken picture.
made_of: Information Control; Lying

name: FOG
short_definition: Fear, a sense of debt, and guilt layered around a request until saying no is frightening, ungrateful and cruel all at once.
made_of: Fear Installation; Obligation Hooks; Guilt-Tripping
sources: Susan Forward (1996). Emotional Blackmail. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL1929398W

name: Idealize-Devalue-Discard Cycle
short_definition: A three-stage arc. Someone is first placed on a pedestal, then steadily criticized and put down, and finally dropped.
made_of: Love Bombing; Pedestal Ploy / The Exception Script; Contempt; Sudden Devaluation

name: Pig Butchering (Long-Con Digital Fraud)
short_definition: A slow online fraud where a stranger wins your trust over weeks or months, then steers you into a fake investment or money loss.
made_of: Social Engineering; Manufactured Intimacy; Future Faking; Bait and Switch; Manufactured Urgency

name: Mobbing
short_definition: A group harasses one person for weeks or months, most often at work or in a community, and wears down their standing.
made_of: Ostracism; Smear Campaigns; Preemptive Accusation / Complaint Weaponization
sources: Leymann (1990). Mobbing and Psychological Terror at Workplaces. Violence and Victims. https://doi.org/10.1891/0886-6708.5.2.119

name: Information Cascades
short_definition: A belief or reputation spreads because each person sees others accepting it, so agreement takes the place of anyone checking whether it is true.
sources: Bikhchandani et al. (1992). A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades. Journal of Political Economy. https://doi.org/10.1086/261849

name: Trauma Bonding
short_definition: A strong attachment that grows through cycles of hurt, then comfort from the same person. Fear and closeness become tangled together.
sources: Dutton and Painter (1993). Emotional Attachments in Abusive Relationships: A Test of Traumatic Bonding Theory. Violence and Victims. https://doi.org/10.1891/0886-6708.8.2.105; Patrick Carnes (1997). The Betrayal Bond. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL2654209W

name: Approval Addiction Cultivation
short_definition: Coming to depend on one person's approval, often built through warmth that comes and goes unpredictably. In the end their reaction counts for more than your own judgment.

name: Fawning
short_definition: Responding to a threatening person by pleasing them, agreeing and shrinking yourself, as an automatic way to stay safe.
sources: Pete Walker (2013). Complex PTSD. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL19987839W

name: Identity Erosion
short_definition: Inside a relationship, your tastes, opinions, limits and friendships slowly fade, until the person you used to be is hard to find.

name: Internalized Conditioning
short_definition: Following rules and reactions that once came from another person. Now they are enforced from inside your own head, even when that person is nowhere near.

name: Learned Helplessness
short_definition: Repeatedly telling someone they could not cope alone, until they start to believe it and stop trying.
sources: Seligman and Maier (1967). Failure to escape traumatic shock. Journal of Experimental Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0024514

name: Pre-Punishment
short_definition: You hold yourself back before anyone else can, by not applying, speaking or trying, because past experience taught you that being seen gets punished.

name: Self-Gaslighting Induction
short_definition: The habit of doubting your own memory and perception on reflex, long after anyone else has needed to challenge it.

name: Silence Installation
short_definition: A learned inability to speak about specific things. Naming them brings dread, because raising them has repeatedly cost more than staying quiet.

name: Group Consolidation
short_definition: Publicly punishing one person harshly enough that everyone watching learns what disagreement will cost them.

name: Behavior Control
short_definition: Setting rules about what another adult may wear, where they may go and who they may see, and enforcing them.
made_of: Time Control; Mobility Control; Sleep Deprivation; Enforcing Trivial Demands; Micromanagement; Body Autonomy Violations
sources: Steven Hassan (1988). Combating Cult Mind Control. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL4475504W

name: Emotion Control
short_definition: Rewarding the feelings a person is allowed to show and punishing or shaming the rest, until they act out emotions instead of reporting them.
made_of: Shame Installation; Fear Installation; Guilt-Tripping; Toxic Positivity / Weaponized Optimism; Emotional Invalidation
sources: Steven Hassan (1988). Combating Cult Mind Control. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL4475504W

name: Information Control
short_definition: Narrowing what someone reads, hears and learns, and who they talk to, so one person's account becomes the main version of events they have.
made_of: Gatekeeping; Compartmentalization; Lying by Omission / Gaslighting by Omission; Narrative Monopoly; Controlled Communication; Echo Chamber Construction
part_of_patterns: Milieu Control; Strategic Deception (Denial & Deception / D&D)
sources: Steven Hassan (1988). Combating Cult Mind Control. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL4475504W

name: Monitoring & Surveillance
short_definition: Demanding constant access to a person's phone, messages and movements. Every part of their day has to be explained.
made_of: Location Tracking; Device Access Demands; Omnipresence / Demonstrating Omnipotence; Response-Time Policing; Smart-Home Coercion
sources: Evan Stark (2007). Coercive Control. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL2982769W

name: Post-Truth Epistemic Manipulation
short_definition: A flood of contradictions and denials that wears down belief in knowable facts, until people trust no source and nobody can be held to account.
made_of: Repetition as Truth; Gish Gallop / Firehose of Falsehood; False Consensus / Social Proof Pressure
sources: Lee C. McIntyre (2018). Post-Truth. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL19744673W

name: Thought Control
short_definition: Controlling the words, explanations and conclusions a person may use, so doubt is labeled a symptom and only one reading of events is allowed.
made_of: Loaded Language; Thought-Stopping Clichés; Sacred Science; Doctrine Over Person; Phobia Indoctrination / Catastrophizing
sources: Steven Hassan (1988). Combating Cult Mind Control. https://openlibrary.org/works/OL4475504W

name: Dark Patterns (AI-Adaptive)
short_definition: Screen designs that push people into purchases, data sharing or consent they did not intend, and that change to fit each user's apparent weaknesses.
made_of: Manufactured Urgency; Manufactured Scarcity; Buried Consent; Gamified Compulsion; Algorithmic Manipulation
sources: Mathur et al. (2019). Dark Patterns at Scale Findings from a Crawl of 11K Shopping Websites. Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction. https://doi.org/10.1145/3359183

name: The "Good Woman Program"
short_definition: Unspoken rules reward women for going along and giving things up, and make them pay for being direct, setting boundaries or taking up space.
made_of: Conditional Love; Intermittent Reinforcement / Push-Pull; Negative Reinforcement Traps; Punishment of Boundaries; Withholding / Silent Treatment

name: Gaslighting
short_definition: Repeatedly denying what someone saw, heard or remembers until they stop trusting their own account of events.
made_of: Countering; Revisionist History; Minimization; Deflection; Lying by Omission / Gaslighting by Omission
sources: Sweet (2019). The Sociology of Gaslighting. American Sociological Review. https://doi.org/10.1177/0003122419874843

name: Lying
short_definition: Saying something the speaker knows to be untrue so that another person will believe it and act on it.
made_of: Countering; Revisionist History; Lying by Omission / Gaslighting by Omission; Half-Truth Framing; Forged Screenshots / Edited Evidence
sources: DePaulo et al. (1996). Lying in everyday life. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.70.5.979

name: Institutional Betrayal
short_definition: An institution that people depend on fails to prevent harm or to treat them fairly afterward, adding a second injury.
made_of: Willful Blindness as Complicity; Victim Blaming; Manufactured Closure; Visible Impunity
sources: Smith and Freyd (2014). Institutional betrayal. American Psychologist. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037564
